# A test reaches a node whose `#id` is named like a component the package
# declares. The id does not shadow the component -- `pair` still renders `box`
# by that name -- but the node still has a handle, which is what the splice of
# `cell` is recorded under and what `c.box.got` is pointed through. Without one
# the read reached each target as a member nothing declares.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component box ui.node {
    ui.text(value="box")
}

component cell(name string) ui.node {
    var got = name
}

component pair ui.node {
    cell #box(name="a")
    cell #other(name="b")
    box()
}

func testAnIdNamedLikeAComponent(t test.Test, c pair) {
    t.assert(c.box.got == "a")
    t.assert(c.other.got == "b")
}

  ]
}
